rv.q: This is a characteristically high-octane version of Ibsen's play: loud, modern and led by screen stars Alicia Vikander and Andrew Lincoln.
And yet the overall results this time feel more mixed.

Would you dump a husband as sexy as Andrew Lincoln? … The Walking Dead star makes it difficult to empathise with Ibsen’s straying heroine in The Lady from the Sea … The snag is that the staging, by Australian hotshot Simon Stone (with semi-abstract design by Lizzie Clachan), leaves his cast first high and dry on an exposing platform, then...

Alicia Vikander is drowned out … Andrew Lincoln is tremendous in the lead role, but his Hollywood co-star is frequently inaudible — and Simon Stone’s Ibsen update is relentlessly self-aware … There are plenty of sharply observed modern-day moments in Simon Stone’s Ibsen rejig, not to mention a tremendous star turn from Andrew Lincoln and a...
Stone has lost sight of what this play's actually about.
It is a hugely enjoyable evening, full of insight and provocation. If it isn’t quite as revealing as the best of Stone’s work, it’s only because he has set himself a very high bar.
